observations.note: The standard and Expressive inset strokes start absent as keyboard focus begins; the default state layer uses the pinned 10% opacity.
Blur interrupts the growing spatial spring, retaining its current ring width and velocity before the fast effects response moves toward zero.
Refocus reverses the in-flight spring continuously, with standard and Expressive trajectories visibly diverging before both approach their two-stroke focused geometry.
The second blur removes focus, reversing the ring toward zero; no detached outline remains around the owners.
Both inset trajectories have settled at the unfocused endpoint.
The reduced-motion preference shows the final focused two-stroke geometry without the spring travel.
